style: calm, natural hesitations, like explaining to a friend
slides: Okay, before you practice, here's a quick summary of counting.
Everything important, in a few minutes.
Work in stages. How many options at each stage? Multiply.
A restriction? Start with the most restricted position. And a position that's already decided gets one.
Five shirts and four hats? That's twenty outfits. Not nine... adding counts items, not outfits.
And a short list with no pattern? Just list them, and count.
Can items repeat? Then the pool stays full. If not, it shrinks by one at each stage.
n items in a row? That's n factorial. And with factorials, expand only until they cancel.
Know these by sight. So if you see seven hundred twenty, think six factorial.
A big factorial over a small one? That's a run of neighbors.
A sum or a difference? Take out the smaller factorial. And don't forget the one.
Divisible by something? Break every factor into primes, and count.
Handshakes, games, two-way routes... each pair was counted twice. So divide by two.
And a group, where order doesn't matter? Count in order, then divide by k factorial.
Choosing a lot of them? Choose who stays out instead.
Six of seven? Seven ways. Seven of nine? Choose the two who stay out, that's thirty-six. Always count the smaller side.
Can't count it in one go? Split it into cases that don't overlap, and add.
"Not", or "at least one"? Count all of them, and subtract the forbidden ones.
Three-digit codes with at least one seven? All one thousand, minus the seven hundred twenty-nine with no seven.
Objects into boxes? Each object chooses. Four friends, two buses... two to the fourth.
Not sure about a formula? Test it on a tiny case you can draw.
Together? Glue them into a block, then multiply by the order inside. Not together? All, minus together.
Repeated items? Divide by the factorial of each repeat. And a round table? Fix one person... so it's n minus one, factorial.
So, before every question, ask yourself these questions.
And the traps: adding when you should multiply, dividing without a reason, and a zero that can't lead a number.
Good luck. Let's practice.
